title: 📈 Study this strategy before blaming Meta
headline: Spend up 21% from September to October while CPA fell 3%
take: Proof CPMs aren't the whole story: start scaling early, check cost caps daily, holdout-test retention, and build landing pages that match the winning ads.
quote: Some of his biggest accounts increased spend by 21% from September to October

title: 🤖 Shopify is testing commissions for AI shopping referrals
headline: Shopify will pay AI assistants 0.3% of the sales they refer
take: Invite-only for now, but brands on Shop Campaigns can fund a bigger cut. Shopify hasn't said whether paying more moves you up the recommendations.
quote: pays participating AI developers 0.3% on eligible purchases they refer

title: 📦 Shipping small orders into the EU? Your costs just went up.
headline: The EU now adds a €2 fee per item on cheap parcels from outside
take: Lands on top of the €3 customs duty from July, right as holiday orders ship. Check who collects it and whether landed-cost numbers include it.
quote: the EU charges a €2 handling fee per item on low-value parcels

title: 📊 Is your Meta budget spread too thin?
headline: Ad sets under ~50 conversions a week pay about 28% more per purchase
take: Meta's own peak-season guide. Its rule of thumb for how many ad sets you can afford: weekly budget ÷ (cost per result × 50).
quote: fewer than around 50 conversions a week cost about 28% more per purchase

title: 📊 Meta is changing how it counts conversions (yes, right before BFCM)
headline: Meta changes how it counts conversions on 12 November
take: A Pixel feature recovers conversions measured on the customer's device. Pilothouse says leave it on, but take a 7/14/28-day baseline against Shopify first.
quote: Pilothouse’s take: leave it on

title: ⚠️ Meta’s AI is freelancing on your ads
headline: Meta's AI is adding creative advertisers never approved
take: Bookshop.org and agency Exverus found AI images, translations and sitelinks in live ads. Meta's new terms (now from 20 November) make the advertiser responsible.
quote: Meta’s AI is freelancing on your ads

title: 🔎 ChatGPT traffic still has some catching up to do
headline: Google organic still drives 27× the conversions of every LLM combined
take: ChatGPT sent 0.62% as many visits as Google organic across 145M sessions on 100 sites. Watch AI referrals, but don't move budget off Google for them yet.
quote: Google organic still drove 27 times as many conversions as every LLM combined.

title: 💸 Did your customer acquisition cost (CAC) actually go down?
headline: Partnership ads can shift CAC, not cut it
take: On-platform CAC can drop 10–20%, but creator commissions, seeding and management costs may just move it to another line on the P&L.
quote: Some of that CAC may have simply moved to another line on the P&L.

title: 🚀 This brand was spending 30% of its Meta budget on people who’d already bought
headline: One brand was spending 30% of its Meta budget on people who'd already bought
take: Pilothouse cut existing-customer spend to under 5% on a $4M apparel brand; US and Canada sales grew 28% YoY over June to September.
quote: More than 30% of Meta spend was reaching existing customers.

title: 🛍️ Meta is switching on product browsing. Pilothouse says opt out before BFCMStarting October 28, Meta says it will turn
headline: Meta switched product browsing on by default from 28 Oct. Opt out before BFCM
take: Meta says testers saw 3% more conversions, but catalog help behind an ad muddies creative tests right before the peak.
quote: a creative that suddenly looks like a winner may be getting help

title: 📈 A $100M Meta buyer says CPMs nearly doubled for brands without a Labor Day offer
headline: CPMs nearly doubled for brands with no Labor Day offer
take: A $100M-a-year Meta buyer saw his portfolio split: brands with strong offers grew 30%+ YoY; the rest saw CPMs nearly double in three weeks with CTR flat.
quote: Brands without one saw CPMs nearly double in three weeks while CTR held flat

title: 📦 Holiday shipping costs are climbing as a second trade route comes under threat
headline: Holiday shipping costs rise again as a second trade route is threatened
take: Diesel past $6 a gallon and peak fees from UPS (27 Sep), USPS (4 Oct) and Amazon (22 Nov–26 Dec), plus Bab el-Mandeb risk.
quote: Anyone who finished their Q4 shipping math in August gets to open the spreadsheet again.

title: 🇨🇦 Canada added tariffs of up to 50% to U.
headline: Canada's counter-tariffs hit US cosmetics, packaging and appliances
take: Duties of 15%, 25% or 50% on C$27.6B of US-origin goods from 8 September. Check HS codes before shipping US-made products into Canada.
quote: adding duties of 15%, 25%, or 50% to C$27.6 billion of U.S.-origin imports

title: 💡 Social is eating more of the Q4 shopping journey
headline: Social is almost level with search for gift discovery
take: Meta's study of 14,473 holiday shoppers in 18 markets: 37% use social for inspiration vs 41% search; social shoppers are likelier to spend more (49% vs 36%).
quote: Social is nearly tied with search for gift discovery.

title: 🤖 Early ChatGPT ad tests are getting clicks without buyers
headline: Early ChatGPT ad tests: clicks, few buyers
take: One agency spent $415 for a 0.6% CTR and no buyers; another saw 57 clicks in ChatGPT and fewer than 20 GA4 visits. Both ran before August's targeting update.
quote: Early ChatGPT ad tests are getting clicks without buyers

title: 📉 ChatGPT basically stopped citing Reddit this week
headline: ChatGPT stopped citing Reddit almost overnight
take: Reddit's citation share went from about 15% to zero, with brand domains and help centres picking it up. You can't control which sources get cited.
quote: which platforms get cited is out of your control

title: 💰 Meta's now betting on your margin, not just your top line
headline: Meta now optimises for profit and pLTV, not just revenue
take: New Profit and pLTV options beside Value Optimisation send net revenue to Meta, so a 60%-margin sale outranks a 15% one at the same price.
quote: Meta's now betting on your margin, not just your top line

title: 📱 Reels ate half your Instagram ad inventory
headline: Reels now take half of Instagram's ad inventory
take: Reels drive 51% of time on Instagram; video inventory passed half of placements after a 10-point YoY jump, and ads per session rose 8%.
quote: Reels driving 51% of user time on Instagram

title: 💸 Meta beat revenue and lost 4% of its stock anyway
headline: Meta's AI spending could end up in your CPMs
take: Meta raised 2026 expense guidance to $165–169B after Q2; profit fell 14%. Costs like this tend to reach advertisers as Q4 gets expensive.
quote: Spend increases like this have a way of finding their way into CPMs

title: 📉 Google's AI is eating clicks so fast even Reddit's had enough
headline: With an AI Overview, only 8% click a regular result
take: Versus 15% without one, and Reddit is weighing whether to renew its $60M-a-year AI data deal with Google.
quote: Just 8% of people click a regular result when an AI Overview shows up

title: 📈 Import costs are climbing, don't plan on relief
headline: Import costs are rising and relief isn't coming
take: 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods, a permanent 10–12.5% import tariff and oil past $90. Leave margin room for Q3 and Q4.
quote: Leave margin room in Q3 and Q4, and don't bank on any of it easing.

title: 📢 That ad you cut last week for a bad CPA day might've been your best one
headline: The ad you cut for a bad CPA week might have been your best
take: Much of a good ad's work (awareness that turns into direct search later) never shows in CPA, and nearly 70% of searches now end without a click.
quote: a lot of what a good ad does never shows up in CPA at all

title: 💰 Shein and Temu just cut EU ad spend. That's your cheaper auction
headline: Shein and Temu cut EU ad spend after a new €3 parcel fee
take: Google auction data shows both pulling back in Europe, which means cheaper auctions for everyone else there.
quote: That's your cheaper auction

title: 💰 A jewelry brand's April sale outperformed BFCM by 222%
headline: A locked April sale beat the brand's own BFCM by 222%
take: Email-only password sale on a 7-figure jewellery brand, its first promotion since Black Friday: conversion rate +218%, ad spend −35%.
quote: net sales up 222%, conversion rate up 218%, ad spend down 35%

title: The Pilothouse Meta team ran a 14-day lifetime vs. daily budget test on a $50
headline: Lifetime budgets beat daily on a $50M brand: CAC $195 vs $240
take: A 14-day Pilothouse test on a health and wellness brand. Lifetime budgets also lifted CTR (1.27% vs 1.13%).
quote: lifetime budgets brought CAC down to $195 against $240 on daily

title: 📉 Meta got much better at finding people. Much worse at finding buyers.
headline: Meta got better at finding people and worse at finding buyers
take: Reach and new-visitor volume are up while traffic quality is down. The suspicion is Meta's push into Reels and expansion at the expense of intent.
quote: Meta got much better at finding people. Much worse at finding buyers.

title: 🛍️ AI-Referred Orders on Shopify Up 13x Year Over Year
headline: AI-referred orders on Shopify up nearly 13× year on year
take: AI sessions grew more than 8× in Q1 2026; those shoppers convert about 50% better than organic and spend about 14% more per order.
quote: they convert at a 50% higher rate than organics

title: ✌️ Meta aged your best audiences to two years On May 18, Meta raised the max retention on purchase-based custom audience
headline: Meta quietly stretched purchase audiences from 180 to 730 days
take: Existing 180-day audiences auto-expanded on 18 May. Retargeting now reaches two-year-old buyers and exclusions shrink prospecting. Reset each window on purpose.
quote: Almost nobody did.

title: Meta Attribution Change: Why ROAS Dropped 40%
headline: Meta's March attribution change cut reported ROAS by 30–45%
take: Mostly a reporting change from engaged-through attribution. The risk is overcorrecting into a retargeting death spiral; use MER as the north star.
quote: why it’s mostly a reporting issue
